title: Six conjectural realization descriptions
context: Adds a six-way classification programme to CT54/003, 005, 007 and CN D01–D05, which concern particular abelian comparisons.
ledger: LM7 C.1 [Known, the return’s claim; explicit realizations of one Fermat 1-motive]; MPL_14_002-044 M01 [first-pass lead; pre-existing category]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: The numbered Betti–de Rham, Betti–Hodge, Hodge, Betti–Gauss–Manin, Betti–Tate and filtered crystalline descriptions are explicitly conjectural; the sheet does not specify equivalences with precisely defined essential images. Relative to the register’s explicit realizations of one Fermat 1-motive, this sheet adds a general classification question without constructing the proposed functors or proving that arbitrary compatible realization data arise from motives.

ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]

Its qualification “mod isogénie” and its allowance for a finite extension of the local field are substantive restrictions; the supplied context does not resolve these two numbered questions.

title: Filtered crystals require an essential-image condition
context: Differs from CT54/005, 007 and CN D03–D05: their Cartier-duality and F/V calculations concern characteristic-p group schemes, not the local-field essential image.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: Colmez and Fontaine identify weakly admissible filtered \((\varphi,N)\)-modules with semistable \(p\)-adic representations, providing a precise later comparison for part of this programme (Colmez & Fontaine, 2000, Theorem A and §4). The sheet states no weak-admissibility condition and gives only a semilinear operator in its filtered-crystal description, so one must distinguish the crystalline specialization from the broader semistable theorem. That theorem does not establish all six proposed descriptions or classify arbitrary geometric motives.

title: The precise scope of Oda’s comparison
context: Adds a local-field programme to CT54/007 and CN D05; the supplied Oda PDF, Corollary 5.11, printed p. 131, supplies a characteristic-p realization comparison.
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M24a [first-pass lead; rational abelian-realization background]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: Oda’s Corollary 5.11 canonically compares the Dieudonné module of the \(p\)-torsion of an abelian variety over a perfect field of characteristic \(p\) with \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}\), compatibly with the Hodge exact sequence (Oda, 1969, p. 131). This gives a precise comparison behind the question in CT54/007, while the local lift, the rational \(p\)-adic representation and the essential image proposed in 18/005 remain additional problems.

title: The ℓ-adic line in a p-divisible list
context: Differs in coefficient prime: CT44/008 has an ℓ-adic Tate-module statement, whereas CT54/007 and Oda, Corollary 5.11, concern p-torsion.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: The frozen line 24 uses \(\ell\), although the surrounding local classification and the vector space \(N\) in line 20 are \(p\)-adic. For \(\ell\ne p\), a prime-to-\(p\) Tate module of a \(p\)-divisible group cannot retain its \(p\)-primary information; this is a notation or scope question to collate, not permission to replace \(\ell\) by \(p\) in the transcription.

title: Recovering the cyclotomic kernel requires a hypothesis
context: Adds a comparison of two splittings to CT16/052, which gives an analytic Kummer generator, and CT44/008, which uses twisted Tate modules; neither supplies this kernel equality.
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 B04 [first-pass lead; weights and cyclotomic characters]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: The formula \(\varphi(\gamma)=u(\gamma)j_2(\chi(\gamma))^{-1}\) immediately gives \(\varphi=u\) on \(\ker\chi\), but the displayed equality \(\ker u=\ker\chi\cap\ker\varphi\) also requires \(\ker u\subseteq\ker\chi\). A sufficient structural reason would be that the Tate character \(\chi\) factors through the realization \(u\); this condition must be checked before using the asserted quotient and its induced character.

title: An index problem in the associated-graded twist
quote: Twist de Tate sur structures de Hodge mixtes
context: Adds mixed-Hodge twist conventions to CT16/003–006, which treats gradings and projectors, and CT44/008, which uses Tate twists; neither gives this associated-graded formula.
ledger: LM7 C.1 [Known, the return’s claim; integral weights of one 1-motive]; MPL_14_002-044 B04 [first-pass lead; weights and Tate conventions]
body: The general convention \(W_i(E(n))=W_{i+2n}(E)\), \(F^i(E(n))=F^{i+n}(E)\) agrees with a Tate twist of weight \(-2n\) (Deligne, 1971, §2.1.13). Under that convention the associated-graded identity is \(\operatorname{Gr}_i^W(E(-1))\simeq(\operatorname{Gr}_{i-2}^W E)(-1)\), whereas frozen line 14 retains unshifted indices and an incomplete parenthesis; this interpretation belongs in the note and must not replace the recorded formula.

title: Filtrations and splittings have different parameter spaces
context: Adds parabolic and Levi parameter spaces to the Hodge extension in CT54/003, 005; the C-torsors in CT47/003 concern integral transforms and are different objects.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: The asserted map \(\mathrm{Big}\to\mathrm{Fil}\) is modeled on \(G/L\to G/B\), with fibre \(B/L\), giving dimensions \(g-\ell\) and \(g-b\) when \(B\) has Levi factor \(L\) and unipotent radical of dimension \(u=b-\ell\). To justify the assertion one must identify the tensor filtrations of fixed type with these homogeneous spaces and construct the relative unipotent group acting on the splitting space; the existence of splittings for individual filtered vector spaces is insufficient.

title: The two descriptions of Q require clarification
quote: Q = fibré des sous groupes de Lévi
context: Adds a period-torsor construction absent from the supplied context; CT54/003 supplies a Hodge extension but no matching Q, H′ or Levi-space identification.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: Line 6 treats \(Q\) as an \(H^{\prime}\)-reduction of an isomorphism torsor, whereas the margin identifies \(Q\) with the space of Levi subgroups and defines \(H^{\prime}\) as the inverse image of a central Tate \(\mathbf G_m\) in \(B^{\prime}/U^{\prime}\). These descriptions give \(\dim H^{\prime}=u+1\) but a Levi-space dimension of \(u\), so a Tate normalization, a quotient or a change in the use of \(Q\) would have to be specified before the written field bounds could be treated as a proof. This is an interpretation question; the frozen symbols remain unchanged.

ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]

The Weyl-orbit description suggests this approach, but the partly illegible independence sentence does not establish an identification with a modern reflex field. Confidence is medium: the quotient by conjugacy and the Galois-twisted Weyl orbit are visible, while part of the decisive final margin is illegible.

title: The explicit strong period conjecture
context: Adds the written witness requested in context/README.md; CT16/021 concerns the transcendental part of H², CT16/035 concerns Bott periodicity, and CT47/003 has unrelated torsors, with no corresponding period conjecture.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]; no dedicated period-conjecture entry
body: For \(k\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}\), the sheet asks whether \(\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(\alpha,\beta)=g+u\), where \(g=\dim G\) and \(u=\dim U^{\prime}\). The intended equality contains maximal transcendence of the Betti–de Rham comparison \(\alpha\) and an additional independence assertion for the Hodge-splitting comparison \(\beta\), making it stronger than the ordinary period equality \(\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(\mathrm{periods})=\dim G\) (Bost & Charles, 2016, §2.2).

title: The listed consequences follow conditionally from maximality
context: Adds a field-tower calculation absent from the supplied context; CT54/003 concerns an extension of realizations rather than transcendence-degree bounds.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: If the diagram supplies \(\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(\alpha)\le g\) and \(\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(\alpha)}K\le u\), then \(\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=g+u\) forces both inequalities to be equalities. For \(k\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}\), applying additivity in the other towers, with the displayed quotient bounds, yields the intended dimensions \(g-b\) and \(g-\ell\) without providing evidence for the initial strong conjecture. Confidence is high for this conditional calculation because transcendence degree is additive in towers, but only medium for its application here until the two descriptions of \(Q\) are reconciled.

title: The group-generation consequence needs the density interpretation
context: Adds a group-generation consequence to CT16/049, which concerns semisimplicity of a motive category and does not discuss generation by a comparison point.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]

The further assertion that one point \(g\) generates \(G\), under semisimplicity and transcendence of \(\pi\), needs an argument controlling the central torus and the normalization; the displayed dimensions alone do not supply it.

title: Schneider’s theorem does not establish the proposed equality
context: Adds a proposed transcendence consequence absent from the supplied context; CT54/003, 005 gives an abelian de Rham comparison but no Schneider theorem or period-independence claim.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: The cancelled claim of transcendence degree \(3\) for four normalized elliptic periods, with determinant \(1\) as the only relation, is substantially stronger than transcendence of individual periods or the classical CM criterion for an algebraic period ratio. Grothendieck’s published note distinguishes Schneider’s theorem from conjectural algebraic independence of periods and quasiperiods, so the manuscript’s phrase cannot serve as a proof of the displayed degree (Grothendieck, 1966, p. 102, note 10).

ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: The cancelled draft adds \(j\) to the normalized period tuple and predicts total transcendence degree \(4\), while the margin raises a special algebraic-\(\tau\) case and contains a deleted question about \(\pi\) over \(k\). Modern André–Grothendieck formulations count the transcendence of the ground field together with that of the periods through an inequality over \(\mathbf Q\); this is a comparison of formulations, not an identification of the uncertain “pré-minimal” condition or a proof of the manuscript’s equality (Bakker & Tsimerman, 2025, Conjecture 1.2).

title: The live elliptic period conjecture is explicit
quote: degré de transcendance égal à \(\dim G\) (\(4\) ou \(2\)) ?
context: Adds the direct elliptic witness requested in context/README.md; the supplied transcription contains no matching full-period conjecture.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]; no dedicated period-conjecture entry
body: The live sheet distinguishes the non-CM \(\mathrm{GL}_2\) case, predicting degree \(4\), from the CM torus case, predicting degree \(2\). In the modern torsor formulation this is the corresponding Grothendieck period conjecture; the CM elliptic case is known, while the full non-CM degree-\(4\) assertion does not follow from the weaker de Rham–Betti results cited here (Bost & Charles, 2016, §2.2).

title: Generation of the elliptic period locus is weaker than genericity
context: Adds a separate weaker period question absent from CT47/003, whose torsors concern integral transforms, and CT16/049, whose subject is motivic semisimplicity.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: Choose a \(\overline{\mathbf Q}\)-point of the period locus and translate that locus to contain the identity; the smallest algebraic subgroup containing the translate describes the smallest algebraic torsor generated by the period point. For one elliptic curve, the coefficient-field theorem of Kreutz et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 5.13(ii), arXiv v3) supplies an affirmative modern comparison after this torsor identification is made precise. This does not establish that the original period locus is itself the full torsor, or prove the non-CM transcendence degree \(4\).

title: The Hodge-splitting question matches Katz’s later question
context: Adds arithmetic transcendence of the analytic splitting to the de Rham extension in CT54/003, 005 and its discussion in CN D01–D02.
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M24a [first-pass lead; abelian-realization background]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: For a non-CM elliptic curve over \(\overline{\mathbf Q}\), the sheet asks whether its analytic Hodge splitting can descend to algebraic coefficients. Katz asks whether an elliptic curve over a number field whose Hodge decomposition is defined over algebraic coefficients must have CM (Katz, 1976, Question 4.0.8, p. 501). This is a close later literature witness; the sources checked here establish neither a claim of priority nor a current resolution of that converse.

title: The CM margin has an eigenspace proof
quote: si \(C\) est à multiplication complexe … \(h\in\overline Q\) !
context: Adds a special splitting mechanism to CT54/003, 005 and CN D01–D02, which discuss the Hodge extension without this CM argument.
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M24a [first-pass lead; abelian-realization background]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection, not an established period result]
body: After adjoining the CM endomorphisms and their eigenvalues, a non-scalar CM endomorphism acts on \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}\) with two distinct algebraic eigenlines whose complexifications are \(H^{1,0}\) and \(H^{0,1}\). Katz gives this argument explicitly, verifying the CM direction after the necessary extension of the field of definition (Katz, 1976, Lemma 4.0.7, p. 501).

title: An abstract lattice and its comparison embedding are separate data
context: Adds a distinction between the coefficient module and its comparison embedding to the Tate modules in CT44/008 and the analytic Kummer generator in CT16/052.
ledger: LM7 C.1 [Known, the return’s claim; explicit realizations and integral weights]; MPL_14_002-044 B04 [first-pass lead; weights and Tate conventions]
body: Keeping the same abstract integral module while shifting its filtrations is compatible with the written twist convention, but comparison with a complex realization also records the Tate period. Deligne’s lattice \(\mathbf Z(n)=(2\pi i)^n\mathbf Z\) and the manuscript’s residue calculation show why the abstract module and its comparison embedding must be tracked separately (Deligne, 1971, §§2.1.13–2.1.14).
